heading: How do I make an MP4 or MOV clip easier to share?
introduction: Re-encode a supported clip to H.264 video in an MP4 file, with AAC audio when the source has audio. A lower resolution cap can reduce the output, while encoding remains on your device.

sections.heading: Start with a practical resolution
sections.body: Keep original preserves the video dimensions. Choose a 1080p, 720p or 480p cap only when resizing is acceptable; smaller inputs are not upscaled. H.264 output may require even dimensions, so an odd-sized input can require an explicitly selected cap rather than a silent resize.

sections.heading: Check the complete download
sections.body: Play the resulting MP4 with sound, and inspect motion, small text and important details. The original container extension does not guarantee that the source codec is supported. Keep the source for editing or another export.

sections.heading: Allow for browser memory and processing time
sections.body: The first media job downloads about 21 MB of engine code. Video encoding is CPU intensive; long or high-resolution clips can exceed browser memory even below the 200 MB input limit. Jobs stop after five minutes. If processing fails, try a shorter clip or a lower resolution.
